messages:
raj: quick q — how should we surface routing fallbacks in the client API?
Currently we return 200 + header (x-redwood-fallback) and emit internal telemetry. Console wants discrete status buckets to chart fallbacks per route. do we change http codes or keep 200 + richer metadata?

liam: lean towards keeping 200. changing to 4xx/5xx for server-side routing decisions will break lots of SDK retry logic.
We should, however, standardize a header + telemetry enum so console and alerts can rely on it.

anna: +1 on 200 for compatibility. but SDK consumers expect something to indicate non-ideal outcome. a single well-documented header is fine as long as we expose it in SDKs and docs.
What about an explicit body field too for JSON responses so non-HTTP clients can parse easily?

eva: console needs this as a first-class metric: fallback_rate by route/model/tier. Header alone is OK, but telemetry must include a discrete value we can index.
Suggested key: routing.outcome with values: ok, fallback, degraded, queued.

liam: agreed. proposal: keep 200; add header `X-RW-Routing: <outcome>` and body field `routing.outcome` for JSON. emit telemetry event `routing.outcome` with same enum. avoid 4xx/5xx unless it's actually a client/server error.
Also suggestion: include `X-RW-Routing-Variant` with the model/variant used for fallback so we can surface which variant is degrading.

anna: small SDK ergonomics note: add a typed field on response objects like `response.routing?.outcome` and `response.headers['x-rw-routing']` so devs can easily check. I'll add to SDK PR.

sre-oncall: for SRE/alerts we need thresholds: alert when fallback_rate > 5% for 5m for any single customer (or route) and when overall fallback_rate > 10% cluster-wide. Also include a daily digest for customers with recurring degraded outcomes.

raj: sounds good. can we define a minimal contract? i.e. header name, allowed enum values, optional variant string, and a queued retry hint header for rate-based queueing. i'll consolidate into a short RFC.

liam: draft proposal snippet:

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-RW-Routing: fallback
X-RW-Routing-Variant: gpt-3.8-4q
X-RW-Retry-After: 2  # seconds (only for queued outcomes)
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "id": "resp_...",
  "text": "...",
  "routing": {
    "outcome": "fallback",
    "variant": "gpt-3.8-4q",
    "reason": "capacity-limit"
  }
}
```

liam: telemetry event: `routing.outcome` = {"outcome":"fallback","variant":"gpt-3.8-4q","route":"/v1/generate","customer_id":"acct_..."} (emitted as structured event)

anna: SDK PR will map header -> response.routing.*, and add an example in quickstart showing how to opt-in to fail-on-fallback behavior if a customer wants to treat fallback as an error.

eva: console UI notes: add a per-route small card showing fallback % (7d, 24h), top variants used for fallback, and ability to filter by customer tier. Also expose a link from a row to the payload sample for inspection.

infra-bot: heads-up: infra deploy window scheduled tomorrow 03:00 UTC to add `X-RW-Routing` header and start emitting `routing.outcome` telemetry to staging. Will post changelog and migration notes. :robot_face:

raj: thanks — i'll put together the RFC and include the thresholds @sre-oncall asked for. anna can you start the SDK changes once RFC lands?

anna: on it. i'll create a draft PR tonight and tag this thread. :thumbsup:

liam: tiny follow-up — we should document the policy for when we choose 'degraded' vs 'fallback' vs 'queued'. proposed quick rules:
- ok: served from ideal model/variant
- degraded: served from lesser-quality variant but same model family
- fallback: served from different model family (or remote region)
- queued: request placed in queue for capacity, return retry-hint

raj: perfect. that's exactly what the console and docs team need. i'll include those definitions in the RFC.

sre-oncall: please add a trace tag `routing.outcome` on the request span so we can correlate latencies with routing decisions.

liam: done — we'll add the span tag in the runtime change.

raj: awesome. closing loop — RFC + infra deploy + SDK PRs. thanks all.
